RAG: A method where an AI searches external documents to find facts before generating an answer.
LLM: An AI computer program trained on large amounts of text to understand and produce human language.
Retrieval: Finding and pulling out the most relevant piece of information from an external document.
Generation: The process where an AI produces a natural language answer using its writing abilities.
Hallucination: When an AI produces incorrect or made-up information with high confidence.
Chunking: Dividing a large document into smaller, manageable sections or paragraphs for searching.
Embedding: Converting a piece of text into a list of numbers that represents its meaning.
Vector: A list of numbers that shows the meaning and position of a text chunk in mathematical space.
Vector Database: A specialized storage system designed to store vectors and find similar ideas rapidly.
Prompt: The input question, instructions, and context provided to an AI model.
Augment: Adding extra relevant facts and reference text into the prompt to help the AI answer accurately.
Context Window: The maximum amount of text an AI model can read and keep in its working memory at one time.
